cells.tense: You're tending it now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the choosing itself, where direction gets decided
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've been tending up for someone else to see and name — not for approval, for witness. When it's balanced, you'll find that finishing something doesn't leave you empty; letting go of it feels like the point, not the loss.
cells.core: You're tending what you've chosen to grow, and you're doing it on purpose. Not clutching it and not walking away from it — you've picked what deserves your care and you show up for it in form, day after day, in the unglamorous way that actually works. You can hold two demands at once without dropping either, and the care doesn't run you down. That steadiness is the whole of it, and you rarely say so out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what you've chosen, on purpose, without exhausting yourself.

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of it, tending something that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the choosing itself, where direction gets decided
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're holding and set it down for a day, trusting that what's yours will still be there. When it's back in balance, you'll dream from what you've actually lived through instead of what you're afraid is coming — growth without the forcing.
cells.core: You're caring for things ahead of schedule — watering what hasn't been planted, bracing for a harvest that's months off, already deciding what to do about problems no one has brought you. The care is real and the timing isn't; you're spending the tending on a future that hasn't arrived, and the thing in front of you right now gets the leftovers. Growth that's forced isn't growth, it's strain, and you can feel the difference even while you keep pushing.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future that hasn't happened yet, and straining to.

cells.tense: You stood at the door of tending it, and you're still standing there.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the choosing itself, where direction gets decided
cells.ask: Name one thing you still want to grow — something small — and keep hoping for it out loud, to one person. When it's back in balance, the care comes back without exhausting you; you'll hold space for things without having to clutch them.
cells.core: There's something you meant to tend and you never quite started — or you started and set it down when it got hard, and you've been standing at that door ever since. Not lazy, just stopped; the choosing didn't happen, so the tending couldn't. What's missing isn't the capacity for care, it's the willingness to pick the thing and commit to it in form. Somewhere back there you learned it wasn't worth the trouble, and you've been agreeing with that ever since.
cells.sheetLine: You meant to tend it. You never quite started.

cells.tense: You're already tending it — you just haven't signed your name.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the choosing itself, where direction gets decided
cells.ask: Say 'I chose this' about one thing you've been calling just what needed doing — to yourself, once. When it's back in balance, you'll finish things and let them go without grief, because the completion is the point and not the loss.
cells.core: You're already growing something with real care — the ways you show up, what you keep alive, the small daily choices that hold it together — and you describe it as just how things are, or just what needed doing. Nobody asked you to, and you haven't told anyone you did. The tending is running under its own momentum; what's missing is you knowing it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending it. You just haven't said so.
